text:
marta: Heads up — planning a prelaunch webinar + benchmark post. Need a crisp competitive surface vs cloud AI platforms, generic LLM APIs, and self-host infra vendors. Can we iterate a short battlecard and 3 go-to-webinar hooks by EOD tomorrow?

ajay: +1. I sketched a quick table of claims vs competitors, will paste in a sec. want to keep it customer-first (latency/cost/reliability).

sam: Re: webinar hooks — propose: 1) "Predictable Inference Economics", 2) "Operationalizing LLMs at Scale", 3) "Keeping Apps Online When Models Flake" — short demos: 1) cost calc, 2) rollout + canary, 3) auto-fallback.

tess: Love the hook ideas. For battlecard: can we avoid absolute numbers where we don't have citations? Use relative phrasing + a clear callout: "verified latency profiles" and point to our benchmark repo.

amart: @tess agreed — but we do have internal bench numbers for the three demo models. Ajay, paste the short ones.

ajay: Paste: ```
Benchmark snapshot (90th pct, 8k prompt)
Redwood-inference/dedicated (g4dn): 120ms
CloudAPI-X managed endpoint (same GPU): 260ms
OpenHost infra (multi-tenant): 480ms
```

ajay: Note: numbers are demo-only, include footnote: "sample workload; results vary by prompt/seq len/quantization".

lee: For messaging vs cloud vendors: emphasize unified runtime across Hosted/Dedicated/Private + routing/fallback that protects uptime. Short line: "Same API, predictable SLOs — on your terms."

olivia: For sales enablement, can we produce 3x one-liners and an objection handler per competitor class? Example:
- Cloud AI platforms: "Fast to start, expensive at scale — Redwood makes predictable economics a reality." -> Objection handler: "We do offer free trial/POC pricing and an estimator that maps your token mix to projected monthly spend."
- LLM APIs (simple endpoints): "Great for prototyping; lack of ops controls." -> Handler: "We support rollouts, KV/prefix caching, and canary policies to avoid regressions in prod."
- Infra vendors (self-host runtimes): "Own everything; pay ops tax." -> Handler: "If you want full control, Redwood Private gives the control plane + managed runtime for less ops overhead."

marta: Good. Two asks: (1) Draft the 1-pager battlecard with those one-liners + 3 objection handlers; (2) Write the landing copy + 3 webinar subject lines for A/B testing. Who picks each?

sam: I'll take subject lines + live demo script. Draft subjects: A) "Lower inference costs without sacrificing latency", B) "Ship reliable LLM features — no downtime surprises", C) "From prototype to SLA-backed inference"

tess: I'll draft the one-pager battlecard and a short benchmarking appendix.

ajay: I'll produce the short benchmark artifact (incl. commands, dataset snippet) and a small visual for slides: latency bar + cost per 1M tokens.

lee: Ops-bot: can you reserve the webinar slot for Wed next week 11a PT?

ops-bot: deploy-bot: booking checked — Wed next week 11:00 PT available. Meeting room: Zoom Pro account (webinar flow).

olivia: For inbound routing: recommend creating an inbound tag "webinar-prelaunch" that triggers a nurture path: 1) immediate email with benchmark highlights + signup link, 2) 3-day follow-up w/ on-demand demo, 3) SDR touch if account signals > $X ARR. Thoughts?

marta: Perfect. Also add a CTA for Dedicated trials + a Private deployment brief for regulated customers.

sam: Minor nit: marketing visuals should not show raw competitor logos in slide deck — use anonymized labels (e.g., "Cloud X") unless legal ok'd.

tess: Noted. I'll use anonymized labels and call out methodology.

ajay: Quick copy stubs for battlecard top: 
"Why teams pick Redwood for inference"
- Predictable latency and unit economics across Hosted, Dedicated, Private
- Built-in fallbacks and rollout controls to keep apps online
- Ops-friendly: autoscale, KV caching, and model/quantization recommendations

olivia: I'll turn those into 3-sentence buyer-facing blurbs for the landing page.

marta: Timeline/deadlines: 
- Today EOD: tess first draft battlecard; ajay benchmark artifact; sam subject lines + demo script
- Tomorrow noon: olivia landing copy + SDR routing flow; lee confirm webinar Zoom + speakers
- Tomorrow 5pm: review and finalize assets

lee: I'll reach out to product for a 5-min cameo in the webinar and lock speakers.

ops-bot: reminder scheduled: review meeting tomorrow 5pm PT (calendar invite sent).

marta: Awesome — small ask: avoid the phrase "we're cheaper" as primary claim. Frame as "predictable costs and better unit economics for production workloads."

sam: Got it. Will phrase A/B lines accordingly.

olivia: Anything else? Need a quick yes/no on demo model choices: GPT-derivative small (synth), open Llama-ish medium, and a retrieval-augmented chat.

marta: Yes to all three. Keep data and prompts short.

lee: I'll prep runbook for the demo: fallback policy enabled, canary at 10%, and autoscale trigger thresholds.

marta: Thanks team — capture final assets in /marketing/webinar/prelaunch/ and ping me when done. :rocket:
